history.summary: FLAG - NO DOCUMENTED TEMPLE: 'Usri Falls Temple' is not a documented shrine. Usri Falls (also spelled Ushri; 'Ushree' means 'beautiful source') is a waterfall and picnic spot 13 km east of Giridih town on the Tundi road, where the Usri River (a Barakar tributary) drops ~12 metres (39-40 ft) in three separate streams through a steep gorge in dense Parasnath-range forest. The gneissic rocks here are geologically noted. The Jharkhand government has been developing it as a tourist spot along with Khandoli Dam and Parasnath. Keep-or-drop decision needed for a temples dataset; the nearest documented shrine noted by one source is the Rani Sati Mandir near the falls, but no source calls any shrine 'Usri Falls Temple'.

name: Usri Falls Temple
town_description: Giridih, literally 'land of hills', is the headquarters of Giridih district in Jharkhand, a mining town on the Chota Nagpur plateau surrounded by forested plateaus; Usri Falls lies about 13 km east of the town on the Tundi road.
tradition: None (natural waterfall site; not a temple)

travel.airport: Ranchi (Birsa Munda Airport) is the nearest major airport (~190 km); Dhanbad is closer (~50-60 km).
travel.railway: Giridih railway station is the nearest (~13-14 km); taxis, tongas and auto-rickshaws available.
travel.road: 13 km east of Giridih town on the road to Tundi; local three-wheeler auto-rickshaws are the main local transport.

visitor_information.best_time: September to March; monsoon months give the fullest flow.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open natural site; visit during daylight hours.
